title: Operator cheatsheet for sovereign storage scenarios
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operator-facing reference for on-call and ops engineers who need to make quick decisions about where customer data must be stored and how to enforce jurisdictional constraints in Private/Dedicated deployments. This is intentionally terse — think "cheat-sheet + decision tree + actionable commands" rather than an architecture design doc.

Audience:
- On-call SREs and infra operators deploying Private stacks
- Solutions engineers validating contracts with customers
- Partner engineers in channel/on-prem integrators

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- If contract requires 'data at rest in EU only' -> block backups and logs to non-EU buckets, pin model weights to EU region, enforce control-plane IP allowlist to EU management VPC.
- If regulatory requirement is 'no cross-border access (no callouts)' -> enable egress deny on data-plane subnets, implement internal proxy for model telemetry, redact PII before any external telemetry.
- If customer allows 'cross-border processing for model inference but storage in-region' -> allow inference calls to hosted model variants only via regional endpoints with token routing; persist only minimal user identifiers.

Decision tree (common operator scenarios):
1) Customer clause: "All customer data stored and processed within X"
   - If X is a jurisdiction (country/region) -> enforce region-pinning at storage layer and network layer. See enforcement steps.
2) Customer clause: "Backups may be stored in Y region for disaster recovery"
   - If permitted -> ensure encryption keys are region-bound (KMS in-hosted region) and add contractual visibility.
3) Customer clause: "We cannot allow telemetry to be sent outside"
   - If strict -> disable telemetry pipelines or provide a local telemetry sink.

Enforcement checklist (fast actions for operators):
- Storage:
  - Ensure object stores for customer data use region-specific buckets with bucket-level IAM that denies PutObject from non-region service accounts.
  - Verify snapshots/AMI/exports are restricted. Add pre-commit hook in backup workflow to abort cross-region copy.
- Models and runtime artifacts:
  - For Private: pin model artifact registry (S3/GCS path) to customer's region. Use hash-verified image pull to avoid fallback downloads.
  - For Dedicated/Hosted fallbacks: ensure runtime checks deny model pulls from non-authorized registries.
- Networking:
  - Apply egress deny policies on data-plane subnets by default; create explicit allowlists for dependencies that are validated against policy.
  - Control-plane traffic: restrict management plane access to the customer's admin CIDR or a Redwood-managed EU-only control plane when required.
- Key management:
  - Require customer use of region-scoped KMS keys (customer-managed CMKs) for data-at-rest if contract requires.
  - Enforce HSM usage for high-assurance customers; keep key usage logs in-region.
- Logs & telemetry:
  - Route application logs to region-local log collectors. For customers that prohibit sending logs offsite, supply a local syslog/ELK endpoint.
  - Redact PII and remove any raw prompt/response text from telemetry unless explicitly permitted.
- Backups & DR:
  - Default: no cross-region backups. If cross-region DR is contractually allowed, require encrypted-transfer-only and CMK control.

Operator commands / quick verifications (pseudo-commands tailored for our infra):
- Verify bucket region and policy: aws s3api get-bucket-location --bucket <bucket> && aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <bucket>
- Check VPC egress rules: rbacctl show egress --vpc <vpc-id>
- KMS check: aws kms describe-key --key-id <key> --query "KeyMetadata.{Region:MultiRegion}" (confirm region binding)
- Model registry pin: registryctl list-artifacts --model <name> --region eu-west-1 --verify-hash=<sha256>
- Backup pipeline guard: backupctl plan --customer <id> --dry-run (should show "cross-region copy: blocked")

Mapping contractual clauses -> technical control (short matrix):
- "Data stored in X country" -> enforce S3/GCS bucket region + CMK region + serialize audit events in-region
- "No cross-border transfers" -> egress deny, local telemetry sink, no CDN origin fallbacks outside region
- "Logs are allowed offsite but must be encrypted" -> allow syslog forwarder to approved endpoint with TLS + client cert (rotate certs monthly)

Edge cases and gotchas:
- Pseudonymous IDs: storing a user id that can be used to reconstruct identity may still be considered a transfer. Treat pseudonymous identifiers as sensitive unless customer signs off.
- Model weights discovered on fallback: if runtime auto-falls back to a hosted model in another region, the artifact may be cached locally. Add runtime guard so that cache writes for region-pinned customers are denied.
- Third-party integrations (email, payment providers): even if allowed by contract, their data handling can create a cross-border flow. Verify their data residency in vendor onboarding checklist.

Rollout / handoff to customer (what solutions engineers must confirm):
- Confirm exact legal wording and identify to which datasets it applies (prompts, embeddings, logs, backups).
- Map each dataset to a storage resource and tag it with customer:data-residency=<jurisdiction>. This tag is used by infra policies.
- Provide the customer with a short acceptance test: 1) create a record, 2) request a manifest of backups, 3) request that telemetry be disabled and verify no external egress.

Monitoring and detection signals (what to alert on):
- Unexpected cross-region object writes (CloudTrail/Storage audit events with destination != allowed region): Severity P0, trigger immediate rollback and incident.
- Unrecognized model pulls by hosts in a customer's VPC: P1, investigate for fallback behavior.
- Telemetry sink failures (means telemetry may be falling back to external): P2, escalate to on-call infra.

Open questions / items to resolve (notes to self):
- Need a standardized tag schema for "residency-scope" across infra services. Current tags are inconsistent across teams (see jira:RED-2143).
- How do we prove to an auditor that ephemeral KV-caches are not replicated outside region? Need a short audit script and artifact.
- Should we add a per-customer runtime flag that disables remote model fallback globally? (pros: safe; cons: complicates multi-tenant upgrades).

Runbook snippets for common incidents:
- Incident: cross-region backup detected
  1) Identify customer and bucket key from audit logs.
  2) Immediately disable backup job (backupctl disable-job --job <id>).
  3) Snapshot the offending host and revoke temporary credentials.
  4) Notify legal + solutions (include contract clause reference).
  5) Restore backups from a region-locked snapshot and run integrity check.

- Incident: model artifact pulled from non-authorized registry
  1) Kill runtime that pulled artifact.
  2) Remove artifact from local cache and mark runtime for reprovisioning with pinned artifacts.
  3) Create postmortem entry and update registry allowlist.

Documentation & references (quick links):
- Confluence: PD-DataResidency-Design (architecture + decision logs)
- Jira: RED-2143 (residency tagging initiative)
- GitHub: infra/private-deployments#462 (policy-as-code for egress denies)

Short-term todos (for next sprint):
- [ ] Implement tagging linter in infra CI to reject deployments missing residency tags (owner: Jae).
- [ ] Draft auditor checklist for ephemeral caches (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Add runtime flag to disable model fallbacks (investigation spike; owner: Liam).

Notes to operator (final quick tips):
- When in doubt, prioritize "deny until proven allowed" for cross-region actions.
- Keep a copy of the signed customer clause in the incident channel when you take remediation actions.
- Lean on solutions engineering for exact clause interpretation; legal should be looped in before customer-facing statements.

History / provenance:
- Created as a condensed operational companion to the PD-DataResidency-Design confluence page. Iterated during an ops tabletop on 2024-09-12.

End of cheat-sheet. If this is useful, I'll expand the runbook snippets into runnable playbooks (ansible/terraform) and add unit tests for the backup guardrail.
